conventions.convention: Dimension is at least one; the reference measure is a supplied sigma-finite Borel measure, and the endpoint law is a supplied Borel probability measure. Conditional densities are normalized at each time for almost every endpoint.
The continuity equation has sign ∂tρ + div(ρu) = 0. Marginal velocity is endpoint-averaged flux divided by marginal density; the definition assigns no value where that density vanishes.

The Gaussian scale is σt = 1 − (1 − σmin)t with σmin > 0, including σmin > 1. The terminal conditional law is Gaussian smoothing of the endpoint, rather than a point mass. Gaussian interfaces assume AC.
Transport cost is squared Euclidean distance without a factor of one half; optimality is conditional endpoint-map optimality.

Training time has uniform probability measure on [0,1]; B ≥ 1 and N ≥ 0. Each batch is fresh and independent of the pre-batch history, sampled gradients are integrable, and remaining in the parameter domain is assumed.

Sampling uses the exact ODE flow under the additional smooth extension and global Lipschitz bounds. No optimization convergence, target-law equality, numerical accuracy, or computational cost guarantee is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Defines a jointly product-measurable conditional density path normalized for almost every endpoint at every time, a C1 conditional density and flux satisfying the continuity equation, and marginal velocity as mixture flux divided by positive marginal density.

Under the stated positive finite marginal density, finite flux, conditional regularity, local endpoint domination, finite losses and variance constant, and integrable parameter-derivative majorants, both objectives are C1 and LC(θ) = LM(θ) + C, so their parameter gradients agree; the marginal continuity equation also holds.

Under the conditional continuity equation, local C1 regularity and the specified local integrable endpoint bounds, with positive mixture density, time and indicated spatial flux derivatives pass through the endpoint integral and the marginal continuity equation holds.

For a centered Borel probability law μ with finite second moment m2, a ∈ R^d and s > 0, every coupling of μ with the law of a + sX has squared-distance cost at least ‖a‖² + (1 − s)²m2; the affine coupling attains equality.

Assuming AC, the mean-linear, positive-scale affine standard Gaussian interpolation has the displayed Gaussian density and conditional velocity satisfying the continuity equation; its endpoint affine map is quadratic-cost optimal with cost ‖x1‖² + d(1 − σmin)².
The endpoint mixture of a conditional probability-density path is nonnegative and measurable and has reference-measure integral one at every time.

Defines finite fresh-batch conditional squared-loss gradient updates and terminal exact-flow sampling from an independent supplied initial law, with the stated integrability, parameter-domain and additional flow hypotheses.
